channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Veolia CEO: Local Demand Independent from French Turmoil, US Midterms
item.description: he CEO of water and waste management company Veolia said that neither the Democrats victory in the US (its number 2 country) nor the political turmoil in France (which represents 20% of revenue) will change the course of demand for Veolia. That’s after the company reported revenues up 3.1% in the first 9 months of the year. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What Trump’s Midterm Defeat Means for China
item.description:
Donald Trump's defeat in the midterms has created new problems for Xi Jinping.
Rebecca Choong Wilkins explains how a Democratic-controlled US Congress could mean more pressure for China. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Italy Exit Tax Plans Risk Upending Years Spent Courting Rich
item.description: For about a decade, Italy has been on a drive to attract the global rich and bring back Italian expats with huge tax exemptions. Now it’s sending mixed messages.
item.dc:creator: Alessandra Migliaccio and Sonia Sirletti

item.title: Assessing the 2026 US Midterm Results: The Energy Angle
item.description: High gasoline and diesel prices, low consumer confidence, prediction markets and history all pointed to major gains for Democrats heading into the November 3 US elections. In this snap webinar held the morning post-vote, BloombergNEF reviewed the Blue Wave and offered early thoughts on the implications for the global energy sector. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Paggi: Can’t React to Trump Rhetoric Amid Daily Changes
item.description: Oil extended its decline as markets bet the US midterm results could reduce the risk of renewed fighting with Iran. Democrats have taken control of both chambers of Congress, while President Trump says he has no immediate plans for fresh strikes. Livia Paggi, Senior MD Strategy & Risk Advisory at JS Held spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on Horizons Middle East & Africa about the likelihood of reescalation in the Middle East. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ayub: US Midterms, Geopolitical Risks Drove Selloff
item.description: A stock-rotation trade fueled by the US midterm elections has swept Asia. Mehvish Ayub, Head of Managed Solutions Advisory Dubai at Bank of Singapore spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on Horizons Middle East & Africa. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Robinhood: New US Congress to Bring Proper Crypto Rules
item.description: Robinhood is expanding into the Middle East, with plans to launch its retail investing platform from a new regional headquarters in Dubai next year. Johann Kerbrat, Robinhood's SVP and Crypto and International General Manager spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on Horizons Middle East & Africa about their expansion but also the impact of the US midterms on crypto. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ANC Loses Ground in South African Municipal Vote, Modeling Shows
item.description: The African National Congress, South Africa’s biggest political party, appears to have hemorrhaged support in Wednesday’s municipal elections, modeling based on the early results shows.
item.dc:creator: Mike Cohen

item.title: Korea Crushed as China Cheers US Midterm: Market Analysis
item.description: Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson, Tom Mackenzie and Paul Dobson break down today's key themes for analysts and investors on "Bloomberg: The Opening Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: JD Vance Breaks With Trump on Iran and Israel After US Midterms Collapse
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
The Republican Party’s generational collapse in this week’s midterm elections ushered in a wave of finger-pointing largely aimed at the Oval Office, exposing deep fissures within the party and opening the door for 2028 hopefuls to hone their message.
Brent oil pushed lower after tumbling more than 8% in the previous session as investors bet that a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections could accelerate efforts to end the war in the Middle East.
Today's guests: Bernd Montag, Siemens Healthineers, CEO; Hetal Mehta, St James’s Place, Chief Economist; Melanie Kreis, DHL Group, CFO (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Did Roy Cohn Frame Ethel Rosenberg? Her Sons' 50-Year FOIA Quest
item.description:
On the Disclosure podcast, how a 50-year FOIA campaign changed the public understanding of the most notorious Cold War espionage case.
In 1953, the US executed Julius and Ethel Rosenberg on charges of conspiring to pass atomic bomb secrets to the Soviets. Their sons, then 6 and 10 years old, have spent a half-century requesting documents the US and prosecutor Roy Cohn used to build its case against their parents. Michael and Robert Meeropol join Jason and Matt to discuss documents from the government's files that contradict the US case against Ethel Rosenberg and have led them to seek a presidential exoneration. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: JD Vance Criticizes Iran War as GOP Blame Game Starts
item.description: Vice President JD Vance distanced himself from President Donald Trump and the war against Iran as the Republican Party’s generational collapse in the midterm elections ushered in a wave of finger-pointing largely aimed at the Oval Office. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Audits Australia’s Canola Supply in Sign of Trade Thaw
item.description: Chinese officials traveled to Australia in late October to audit the country’s canola supply chain, according to Agriculture Minister Julie Collins, the latest sign that the two countries are moving toward normalizing trade in the crop.
item.dc:creator: Ben Westcott

item.title: Stock Rotation Hits Chips, Boosts China
item.description: A stock-rotation trade fueled by the US midterm elections swept Asia, denting regional chipmakers and boosting unfavored markets from China to Australia. Bloomberg's Anthony Stephens reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oil Pushes Lower on Hopes to End US-Iran War
item.description: Brent oil extended its slide after tumbling more than 8% in the previous session as investors bet that a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections could accelerate efforts to end the war in the Middle East. Bloomberg's Onur Ant reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: France Braces for Marches and Strikes Amid Stalled Budget
item.description: France is bracing for a day of strikes and demonstrations over the cost of living, extending more than a month of protests, as parliamentary talks over next year’s budget remain deadlocked.
item.dc:creator: Ania Nussbaum

item.title: How the US Midterms Reshaped the Risk of US Iran Strike
item.description: Bloomberg's Abeer Abu Omar says the likelihood of US military action against Iran remains uncertain following the midterm elections, even as crude prices decline on market expectations that an immediate attack is unlikely. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hong Kong Jails Joshua Wong for a Decade in Collusion Case
item.description: A Hong Kong court sentenced prominent pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong to 10 years in prison for his second national security conviction, extending his incarceration just two months before he was due to be freed.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan

item.title: South Korea to Send Navy Assets to Mideast After US Midterms
item.description: South Korea is preparing to send more military assets to the Middle East and widen its anti-piracy operations, months after President Donald Trump urged the Asian ally to join efforts to secure the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Supreme Court’s Alito Repeated He Won’t Retire Over Election
item.description: Samuel Alito has said that Tuesday’s sweeping election win by Democrats didn’t change his plans to remain on the Supreme Court when the new Congress takes office, according to a person who spoke with the justice.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr
